claim_verdicts.evidence: git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:docs/team/sprint-example.md, lines 12-18: header 'Việc | Người nhận | Ước lượng | Trạng thái cuối sprint'; rows: 'API POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel | Dev 1 | 3', 'Nút "Hủy đơn"... | Dev 2 | 3', 'Chặn hủy đơn đã thanh toán | Dev 1 | 2', 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy | Dev 3 | 2', 'Sửa lỗi tổng tiền sai ở đơn nhiều dòng | Dev 4 | 1'. 3+3+2+2+1 = 11.

Line 17: 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy | Dev 3 | 2 | Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau'. Sprint review: 'Việc "Ngừng gửi thông báo" chưa xong nên không được trình diễn — chưa xong thì chưa tính, dù đã viết gần hết code.' The file gives no reason why the item did not finish (see issues on §6/§7).

git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:docs/team/kanban-board-example.md: column header is 'Việc cần làm | Đang làm (giới hạn 2) | Chờ review (giới hạn 2) | Xong'; no estimate column and no number next to any item anywhere in the file.

Consistent with Scrum Guide 2020 (WebFetch summary): 'The Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing.'; 'Selecting how much can be completed within a Sprint may be challenging... the more confident they will be in their Sprint forecasts.'; 'The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.' The Guide does not mandate numeric estimates. 'Sometimes wrong in both directions' follows from 'made before the work'. Accepted as opinion.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and not supported by the repo: sprint-example.md says only that the item was 'Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau' and 'đã viết gần hết code'. Nothing says a problem appeared, let alone one 'nobody could have seen at planning'. The retrospective's 'Cần sửa' is 'nhận việc phụ thuộc vào một người duy nhất', which is not an unforeseeable problem.
issues.quote: when an item estimated at 2 turns up a problem nobody could have seen at planning, and takes longer, as happened in Sprint 14.
issues.fix: Replace with: "You notice this in Sprint 14: an item estimated at 2 did not finish, and nothing in the sprint file blames the estimate or the person who gave it." If a cause is kept, add it to claims with the repo line that supports it.

issues.text: Unlisted claim stated as fact about Sprint 14: the repo gives no reason the item did not finish, so 'the work turned out bigger than it looked' is invented. The example retro sentence also invents a fact ('the notification code we know least'); the real retro names a different lesson. Same invented cause in quiz q2 explanation 'One item growing'.
issues.quote: the work turned out bigger than it looked, which estimates are expected to do sometimes.
issues.fix: §7 answer: "the work may have turned out bigger than it looked, which estimates are expected to do sometimes." Example sentence: "this item depended on one person; next time, make sure two people know the code before we size it." q2 correct explanation: replace 'One item growing' with 'One item not finishing'.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: sprint-example.md has no account of the planning meeting and does not say the numbers were used to decide the five items fit. It is the lesson's interpretation presented as a fact from the file.
issues.quote: Those numbers let the team decide, at planning, that these five items fit into two weeks.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Numbers like these are what a team uses at planning to judge whether five items fit into two weeks." Add to claims as kind opinion, section 5.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: claim 3 covers only the missing column. The reason given ('so it has less need to size each item') is not in kanban-board-example.md, which explains why there is no sprint, not why there is no estimate. Quiz q5 depends on this sentence.
issues.quote: it limits what is in progress instead, so it has less need to size each item before it starts.
issues.fix: Add a claim (kind opinion, section 5): "A team that does not plan a batch of work in advance has less need to size each item before it starts; the Kanban file gives no reason of its own." The sentence itself may stay.

issues.text: Unlisted behavioural claim stated as a certainty. The pinned sources (Scrum Guide 2020, repo) say nothing about padding. Quiz q4 is built on it.
issues.quote: You notice this when a team that is held to its estimates starts padding every number, and the estimates stop being useful for planning.
issues.fix: Replace with: "You notice this when a team that is held to its estimates starts padding its numbers, and the estimates stop being useful for planning" only after adding it to claims as kind opinion, section 6; or hedge to 'can start padding'.

issues.text: Absolute 'cannot ... without estimates' goes past the outline ('without knowing roughly how big each one is relative to the others') and past the Scrum Guide 2020, which does not require estimates ('Selecting how much can be completed within a Sprint may be challenging').
issues.quote: what the team cannot do without estimates is decide how many stories to take into a sprint.
issues.fix: Replace with: "what the team cannot do without some idea of each story's size is decide how many stories to take into a sprint." (Summary line 4 already says it this way.)

issues.text: Generic statement about sprint planning fixes the sprint at two weeks; Scrum Guide 2020: sprints 'are fixed length events of one month or less'. Two weeks is only Sprint 14's length.
issues.quote: how many of the waiting stories fit into the next two weeks.
issues.fix: Replace with: "how many of the waiting stories fit into the next sprint."

issues.text: The file says only that the item was not demonstrated and not counted; 'did not treat that as a broken promise' attributes an attitude the file does not record.
issues.quote: The review did not treat that as a broken promise: unfinished work is simply not counted as done yet.
issues.fix: Replace with: "At the sprint review it was simply not shown: unfinished work is not counted as done yet."

issues.text: The situation mirrors Sprint 14 (3, 3, 2, 2, 1), whose five items include a bug fix ('Sửa lỗi tổng tiền sai'), not only stories; §5 correctly says 'items'.
issues.quote: The product owner reads out five stories
